learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to problem-solving.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Know and apply the ethical and legal aspects related to data processing and the application of obtained knowledge.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Analyze data from complex phenomena by applying statistical techniques and probability calculation.
Understand and correctly apply exploratory data analysis and statistical modeling techniques, evaluating model quality, validating them, and interpreting them.
Know the main data preprocessing techniques and determine the most appropriate in each context.
Perform a principal component analysis and know the main methods.
Perform a factorial analysis of a dataset, both exploratory and confirmatory.
Know the different multidimensional scaling methods and the differences between them.
Perform a correspondence analysis on a dataset.
Handle the different concepts and methodologies within discriminant analysis with fluency.
Adequately distinguish between all the previous techniques and apply the appropriate one in each context.

syllabus_topics: Data preprocessing techniques. Motivation. Preprocessing tasks: cleaning, integration, transformation, reduction, and discretization of data.
Principal component analysis. Correlation-based method. Covariance-based method. Limitations.
Multidimensional scaling (MDS). Classical and non-metric models.
Discriminant analysis. Discriminant functions. LDA, incremental LDA, multiclass LDA, and high-dimensional LDA methods.

assessment_methods.method: Participation in forums and activities on the Virtual Campus

assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call is calculated as: 0.05 * Attendance and participation + 0.10 * Participation in forums and Virtual Campus activities + 0.40 * Practical evaluation + 0.45 * Final theoretical exam. No minimum grade is established for any assessable element. To pass, a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required. In the extraordinary call of July, students may keep the grades obtained in the ordinary call. In the extraordinary call of January, evaluation will consist of a theoretical-practical final exam, accounting for 100% of the final grade. For differentiated evaluation, students must choose at the beginning of the course between continuous evaluation or a single theoretical-practical test accounting for 100% of the final grade.
